passages.text: Now a worthless man named Sheba son of Bichri, a Benjamite, happened to be there, and he blew the ram’s horn and shouted: “We have no share in David, no inheritance in Jesse’s son. Every man to his tent, O Israel!”
passages.sermon:
Sheba was a worthless man.
His father was Bichri.
Sheba was from the tribe of Benjamin.
Sheba was present at that place.
Sheba blew a ram’s horn.
Sheba shouted to the people.
Sheba said, “We have no share in David.
We have no inheritance in Jesse’s son.
Everyone in Israel, go to your own tent.”
passages.original: וְשָׁ֨ם נִקְרָ֜א אִ֣ישׁ בְּלִיַּ֗עַל וּשְׁמ֛וֹ שֶׁ֥בַע בֶּן־ בִּכְרִ֖י אִ֣ישׁ יְמִינִ֑י וַיִּתְקַ֣ע בַּשֹּׁפָ֗ר וַ֠יֹּאמֶר אֵֽין־ לָ֨נוּ חֵ֜לֶק בְּדָוִ֗ד וְלֹ֤א נַֽחֲלָה־ לָ֙נוּ֙ בְּבֶן־ יִשַׁ֔י אִ֥ישׁ לְאֹהָלָ֖יו יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: So all the men of Israel deserted David to follow Sheba son of Bichri. But the men of Judah stayed by their king all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
All the men of Israel left David.
They followed Sheba son of Bichri.
Sheba was a Benjamite.
The men of Judah stayed with their king David.
They stayed with him from the Jordan River to Jerusalem.
passages.original: וַיַּ֜עַל כָּל־ אִ֤ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵאַחֲרֵ֣י דָוִ֔ד אַחֲרֵ֖י שֶׁ֣בַע בֶּן־ בִּכְרִ֑י וְאִ֤ישׁ יְהוּדָה֙ דָּבְק֣וּ בְמַלְכָּ֔ם מִן־ הַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן וְעַד־ יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: When David returned to his palace in Jerusalem, he took the ten concubines he had left to care for the palace, and he placed them in a house under guard. He provided for them, but he no longer slept with them. They were confined until the day of their death, living as widows.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David returned to his palace in Jerusalem.
David had ten concubines.
He had left these ten concubines to care for the palace.
David took these ten concubines.
He placed them in a guarded house.
David provided for their needs.
He did not sleep with them anymore.
The ten concubines lived in confinement.
They remained confined until they died.
They lived as widows.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֨א דָוִ֣ד אֶל־ בֵּיתוֹ֮ יְרֽוּשָׁלִַם֒ וַיִּקַּ֣ח הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ אֵ֣ת עֶֽשֶׂר־ נָשִׁ֣ים׀ פִּלַגְשִׁ֡ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִנִּיחַ֩ לִשְׁמֹ֨ר הַבַּ֜יִת וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֤ם בֵּית־ מִשְׁמֶ֙רֶת֙ וַֽיְכַלְכְּלֵ֔ם וַאֲלֵיהֶ֖ם לֹא־ בָ֑א וַתִּהְיֶ֧ינָה צְרֻר֛וֹת עַד־ י֥וֹם מֻתָ֖ן אַלְמְנ֥וּת חַיּֽוּת׃ס

passages.text: Then the king said to Amasa, “Summon the men of Judah to come to me within three days, and be here yourself.”
passages.sermon:
King David spoke to Amasa.
David was the king of Israel.
Amasa was one of David’s commanders.
David gave Amasa a command.
David said, “Call the men of Judah for me.”
David told Amasa to gather them within three days.
David also told Amasa, “You must be here yourself.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֶל־ עֲמָשָׂ֔א הַזְעֶק־ לִ֥י אֶת־ אִישׁ־ יְהוּדָ֖ה שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֑ים וְאַתָּ֖ה פֹּ֥ה עֲמֹֽד׃

passages.text: So Amasa went to summon Judah, but he took longer than the time allotted him.
passages.sermon:
Amasa was a commander.
David told Amasa to gather the men of Judah.
Amasa went to summon the men of Judah.
Amasa did not return on time.
Amasa took longer than the time David gave him.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ עֲמָשָׂ֖א לְהַזְעִ֣יק אֶת־ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיֵּיחַר מִן־ הַמּוֹעֵ֖ד אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְעָדֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: And David said to Abishai, “Now Sheba the son of Bichri will do us more harm than Absalom. Take your lord’s servants and pursue him, or he will find fortified cities and elude us.”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
Abishai was one of David’s commanders.
David spoke to Abishai.
David said, “Sheba son of Bichri is a threat to us.
Sheba will harm us more than Absalom did.
Take your master’s servants.
Pursue Sheba.
If you do not pursue him, he may find strong, fortified cities.
If Sheba finds these cities, he will escape from us.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ אֶל־ אֲבִישַׁ֔י עַתָּ֗ה יֵ֧רַֽע לָ֛נוּ שֶׁ֥בַע בֶּן־ בִּכְרִ֖י מִן־ אַבְשָׁל֑וֹם אַ֠תָּה קַ֞ח אֶת־ עַבְדֵ֤י אֲדֹנֶ֙יךָ֙ וּרְדֹ֣ף אַחֲרָ֔יו פֶּן־ מָ֥צָא ל֛וֹ עָרִ֥ים בְּצֻר֖וֹת וְהִצִּ֥יל עֵינֵֽנוּ׃

passages.text: So Joab’s men, along with the Cherethites, the Pelethites, and all the mighty men, marched out of Jerusalem in pursuit of Sheba son of Bichri.
passages.sermon:
Joab was a commander in Israel.
Joab had men who served under him.
The Cherethites were a group of skilled fighters.
The Pelethites were also skilled fighters.
There were other mighty men with them.
All these men left Jerusalem together.
They went out to chase Sheba, the son of Bichri.
passages.original: וַיֵּצְא֤וּ אַֽחֲרָיו֙ אַנְשֵׁ֣י יוֹאָ֔ב וְהַכְּרֵתִ֥י וְהַפְּלֵתִ֖י וְכָל־ הַגִּבֹּרִ֑ים וַיֵּֽצְאוּ֙ מִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם לִרְדֹּ֕ף אַחֲרֵ֖י שֶׁ֥בַע בֶּן־ בִּכְרִֽי׃

passages.text: And while they were at the great stone in Gibeon, Amasa joined them. Now Joab was dressed in military attire, with a dagger strapped to his belt. And as he stepped forward, he slipped the dagger from its sheath.
passages.sermon:
Joab and his men stood by the great stone in Gibeon.
Amasa came to meet them there.
Joab wore his military clothes.
Joab had a dagger fastened to his belt.
Joab stepped forward.
Joab drew the dagger from its sheath.
passages.original: הֵ֗ם עִם־ הָאֶ֤בֶן הַגְּדוֹלָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּגִבְע֔וֹן וַעֲמָשָׂ֖א בָּ֣א לִפְנֵיהֶ֑ם וְיוֹאָ֞ב חָג֣וּר׀ מִדּ֣וֹ לְבֻשׁ֗וּ וְעָלוֹ חֲג֥וֹר חֶ֙רֶב֙ מְצֻמֶּ֤דֶת עַל־ מָתְנָיו֙ בְּתַעְרָ֔הּ וְה֥וּא יָצָ֖א וַתִּפֹּֽל׃ס

passages.text: “Are you well, my brother?” Joab asked Amasa. And with his right hand Joab grabbed Amasa by the beard to kiss him.
passages.sermon:
Joab was a commander in David’s army.
Amasa was also a leader in Israel.
Joab spoke to Amasa.
Joab said, “Are you well, my brother?”
Joab used his right hand.
Joab grabbed Amasa by the beard.
Joab did this to kiss Amasa.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יוֹאָב֙ לַעֲמָשָׂ֔א הֲשָׁל֥וֹם אַתָּ֖ה אָחִ֑י וַתֹּ֜חֶז יַד־ יְמִ֥ין יוֹאָ֛ב בִּזְקַ֥ן עֲמָשָׂ֖א לִנְשָׁק־ לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Amasa was not on guard against the dagger in Joab’s hand, and Joab stabbed him in the stomach and spilled out his intestines on the ground. And Joab did not need to strike him again, for Amasa was dead. Then Joab and his brother Abishai pursued Sheba son of Bichri.
passages.sermon:
Amasa did not watch for the dagger in Joab’s hand.
Joab held a dagger.
Joab stabbed Amasa in the stomach with the dagger.
Amasa’s intestines spilled onto the ground.
Joab did not strike Amasa again.
Amasa died from the first blow.
Joab and his brother Abishai left Amasa.
Joab and Abishai chased Sheba son of Bichri.
passages.original: וַעֲמָשָׂ֨א לֹֽא־ נִשְׁמַ֜ר בַּחֶ֣רֶב׀ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּיַד־ יוֹאָ֗ב וַיַּכֵּהוּ֩ בָ֨הּ אֶל־ הַחֹ֜מֶשׁ וַיִּשְׁפֹּ֨ךְ מֵעָ֥יו אַ֛רְצָה וְלֹא־ שָׁ֥נָה ל֖וֹ וַיָּמֹ֑תס וְיוֹאָב֙ וַאֲבִישַׁ֣י אָחִ֔יו רָדַ֕ף אַחֲרֵ֖י שֶׁ֥בַע בֶּן־ בִּכְרִֽי׃

passages.text: One of Joab’s young men stood near Amasa and said, “Whoever favors Joab, and whoever is for David, let him follow Joab!”
passages.sermon:
Joab was a commander in Israel’s army.
Amasa was another leader in Israel.
Joab’s young servant stood by Amasa.
The servant spoke loudly.
He said, “Whoever supports Joab, follow Joab.”
He also said, “Whoever is loyal to David, follow Joab.”
passages.original: וְאִישׁ֙ עָמַ֣ד עָלָ֔יו מִֽנַּעֲרֵ֖י יוֹאָ֑ב וַיֹּ֗אמֶר מִי֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר חָפֵ֧ץ בְּיוֹאָ֛ב וּמִ֥י אֲשֶׁר־ לְדָוִ֖ד אַחֲרֵ֥י יוֹאָֽב׃

passages.text: But Amasa wallowed in his blood in the middle of the road, and when the man saw that all the troops were stopping there, he dragged the body off the road into a field and threw a garment over it.
passages.sermon:
Amasa was a commander in Israel.
Joab killed Amasa with a dagger.
Amasa lay in the middle of the road.
Amasa was covered in his own blood.
A man saw Amasa lying there.
All the people stopped when they saw Amasa.
The man dragged Amasa’s body off the road.
He moved the body into a field.
He threw a garment over Amasa’s body.
Everyone who passed by saw what had happened and stopped.
passages.original: וַעֲמָשָׂ֛א מִתְגֹּלֵ֥ל בַּדָּ֖ם בְּת֣וֹךְ הַֽמְסִּלָּ֑ה וַיַּ֨רְא הָאִ֜ישׁ כִּֽי־ עָמַ֣ד כָּל־ הָעָ֗ם וַיַּסֵּב֩ אֶת־ עֲמָשָׂ֨א מִן־ הַֽמְסִלָּ֤ה הַשָּׂדֶה֙ וַיַּשְׁלֵ֤ךְ עָלָיו֙ בֶּ֔גֶד כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר רָאָ֔ה כָּל־ הַבָּ֥א עָלָ֖יו וְעָמָֽד׃

passages.text: As soon as Amasa’s body was removed from the road, all the men went on with Joab to pursue Sheba son of Bichri.
passages.sermon:
Amasa was dead.
Someone removed Amasa’s body from the road.
Joab was the commander of the army.
All the men followed Joab.
They left the place.
They went to chase Sheba son of Bichri.
passages.original: כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הֹגָ֖ה מִן־ הַֽמְסִלָּ֑ה עָבַ֤ר כָּל־ אִישׁ֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י יוֹאָ֔ב לִרְדֹּ֕ף אַחֲרֵ֖י שֶׁ֥בַע בֶּן־ בִּכְרִֽי׃

passages.text: Sheba passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel-beth-maacah and through the entire region of the Berites, who gathered together and followed him.
passages.sermon:
Sheba was a leader who rebelled against King David.
Sheba traveled through every tribe of Israel.
He went to Abel-beth-maacah.
He also passed through the land of the Berites.
The Berites gathered together.
They followed Sheba.
passages.original: וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֞ר בְּכָל־ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אָבֵ֛לָה וּבֵ֥ית מַעֲכָ֖ה וְכָל־ הַבֵּרִ֑יםס וַיִּקָּלְהוּ וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ אַף־ אַחֲרָֽיו׃

passages.text: And Joab’s troops came and besieged Sheba in Abel-beth-maacah and built a siege ramp against the outer rampart of the city. As all the troops with Joab were battering the wall to topple it, a wise woman called out from the city, “Listen! Listen! Please tell Joab to come here so that I may speak with him.”
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of the army.
Joab’s troops came to the city of Abel-beth-maacah.
They surrounded the city.
They besieged Sheba inside the city.
Joab’s men built a siege ramp against the outer wall of the city.
The ramp stood against the city’s fortification.
All the people with Joab tried to destroy the wall.
They wanted to make the wall fall down.
A wise woman was inside the city.
She called out from the city.
She said, “Listen! Listen!”
She said, “Please tell Joab to come here.”
She said, “I want to speak with him.”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ וַיָּצֻ֣רוּ עָלָ֗יו בְּאָבֵ֙לָה֙ בֵּ֣ית הַֽמַּעֲכָ֔ה וַיִּשְׁפְּכ֤וּ סֹֽלְלָה֙ אֶל־ הָעִ֔יר וַֽתַּעֲמֹ֖ד בַּחֵ֑ל וְכָל־ הָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶת־ יוֹאָ֔ב מַשְׁחִיתִ֖ם לְהַפִּ֥יל הַחוֹמָֽה׃ וַתִּקְרָ֛א אִשָּׁ֥ה חֲכָמָ֖ה מִן־ הָעִ֑יר שִׁמְע֤וּ שִׁמְעוּ֙ אִמְרוּ־ נָ֣א אֶל־ יוֹאָ֔ב קְרַ֣ב עַד־ הֵ֔נָּה וַאֲדַבְּרָ֖ה אֵלֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: When he had come near to her, the woman asked, “Are you Joab?” “I am,” he replied. “Listen to the words of your servant,” she said. “I am listening,” he answered.
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of David’s army.
A wise woman called Joab to speak with her from the city.
Joab came near to the woman.
The woman asked, “Are you Joab?”
Joab replied, “I am.”
The woman said, “Listen to the words of your servant.”
Joab answered, “I am listening.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְרַ֣ב אֵלֶ֔יהָ וַתֹּ֧אמֶר הָאִשָּׁ֛ה הַאַתָּ֥ה יוֹאָ֖ב וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אָ֑נִי וַתֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ שְׁמַע֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י אֲמָתֶ֔ךָ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר שֹׁמֵ֥עַ אָנֹֽכִי׃

passages.text: Then the woman said, “Long ago they used to say, ‘Seek counsel at Abel,’ and that is how disputes were settled.
passages.sermon:
A wise woman spoke to Joab.
She said, “People once said something important about this city.
They said, ‘Ask for advice at Abel.’
People came here to seek counsel.
They settled their disputes in this place.
This is how matters were finished in Abel.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֖אמֶר לֵאמֹ֑ר דַּבֵּ֨ר יְדַבְּר֤וּ בָרִֽאשֹׁנָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר שָׁאֹ֧ל יְשָׁאֲל֛וּ בְּאָבֵ֖ל וְכֵ֥ן הֵתַֽמּוּ׃

passages.text: I am among the peaceable and faithful in Israel, but you are trying to destroy a city that is a mother in Israel. Why would you swallow up the LORD’s inheritance?”
passages.sermon:
I am a peaceable person in Israel.
I am faithful to Israel.
You are trying to destroy a city in Israel.
This city is like a mother in Israel.
Why do you want to destroy the LORD’s inheritance?
passages.original: אָנֹכִ֕י שְׁלֻמֵ֖י אֱמוּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אַתָּ֣ה מְבַקֵּ֗שׁ לְהָמִ֨ית עִ֤יר וְאֵם֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לָ֥מָּה תְבַלַּ֖ע נַחֲלַ֥ת יְהוָֽה׃פ

passages.text: “Far be it!” Joab declared. “Far be it from me to swallow up or destroy!
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of Israel’s army.
Joab answered.
Joab said, “Never let it be!”
Joab said, “I would never swallow up this city.”
Joab said, “I would never destroy it.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַן יוֹאָ֖ב וַיֹּאמַ֑ר חָלִ֤ילָה חָלִ֙ילָה֙ לִ֔י אִם־ אֲבַלַּ֖ע וְאִם־ אַשְׁחִֽית׃

passages.text: That is not the case. But a man named Sheba son of Bichri, from the hill country of Ephraim, has lifted up his hand against the king, against David. Deliver him alone, and I will depart from the city.” “Look,” the woman replied, “his head will be thrown to you over the wall.”
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of Israel’s army.
A wise woman spoke to Joab.
She said, “That is not the case.”
Sheba son of Bichri is a man from the hill country of Ephraim.
Sheba has lifted his hand against King David.
You want only Sheba.
Give Sheba to you alone.
Then you will leave the city.
The woman said to Joab, “Look.”
“We will throw his head to you over the wall.”
passages.original: לֹא־ כֵ֣ן הַדָּבָ֗ר כִּ֡י אִישׁ֩ מֵהַ֨ר אֶפְרַ֜יִם שֶׁ֧בַע בֶּן־ בִּכְרִ֣י שְׁמ֗וֹ נָשָׂ֤א יָדוֹ֙ בַּמֶּ֣לֶךְ בְּדָוִ֔ד תְּנֽוּ־ אֹת֣וֹ לְבַדּ֔וֹ וְאֵלְכָ֖ה מֵעַ֣ל הָעִ֑יר וַתֹּ֤אמֶר הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אֶל־ יוֹאָ֔ב הִנֵּ֥ה רֹאשׁ֛וֹ מֻשְׁלָ֥ךְ אֵלֶ֖יךָ בְּעַ֥ד הַחוֹמָֽה׃

passages.text: Then the woman went to all the people with her wise counsel, and they cut off the head of Sheba son of Bichri and threw it to Joab. So he blew the ram’s horn and his men dispersed from the city, each to his own home. And Joab returned to the king in Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
A wise woman spoke to all the people in the city.
She gave them wise advice.
The people listened to her.
They cut off the head of Sheba son of Bichri.
They threw Sheba’s head to Joab.
Joab was the commander of Israel’s army.
Joab blew the ram’s horn.
The army heard the sound.
The soldiers left the city.
Each man went to his own home.
Joab left the city.
Joab returned to Jerusalem.
Joab went to the king.
passages.original: וַתָּבוֹא֩ הָאִשָּׁ֨ה אֶל־ כָּל־ הָעָ֜ם בְּחָכְמָתָ֗הּ וַֽיִּכְרְת֞וּ אֶת־ רֹ֨אשׁ שֶׁ֤בַע בֶּן־ בִּכְרִי֙ וַיַּשְׁלִ֣כוּ אֶל־ יוֹאָ֔ב וַיִּתְקַע֙ בַּשּׁוֹפָ֔ר וַיָּפֻ֥צוּ מֵֽעַל־ הָעִ֖יר אִ֣ישׁ לְאֹהָלָ֑יו וְיוֹאָ֛ב שָׁ֥ב יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם אֶל־ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס

passages.text: Now Joab was over the whole army of Israel; Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and Pelethites; Adoram was in charge of the forced labor; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the recorder; Sheva was the scribe; Zadok and Abiathar were priests; and Ira the Jairite was David’s priest.
passages.sermon:
Joab commanded the entire army of Israel.
Benaiah was the son of Jehoiada.
Benaiah was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites.
Adoram was in charge of the forced labor.
Jehoshaphat was the son of Ahilud.
Jehoshaphat served as the recorder.
Sheva was the scribe.
Zadok and Abiathar were priests.
Ira was from Jair.
Ira served as priest for David.
passages.original: וְיוֹאָ֕ב אֶ֥ל כָּל־ הַצָּבָ֖א יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּבְנָיָה֙ בֶּן־ יְה֣וֹיָדָ֔ע עַל־ הַכְּרִי וְעַל־ הַפְּלֵתִֽי׃ וַאֲדֹרָ֖ם עַל־ הַמַּ֑ס וִיהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט בֶּן־ אֲחִיל֖וּד הַמַּזְכִּֽיר׃ וְשֵׁיָא סֹפֵ֑ר וְצָד֥וֹק וְאֶבְיָתָ֖ר כֹּהֲנִֽים׃ וְגַ֗ם עִירָא֙ הַיָּ֣אִרִ֔י הָיָ֥ה כֹהֵ֖ן לְדָוִֽד׃ס
